newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK defers licensing of cordless access services.
newsitem.headline: HK defers licensing of cordless access services.

text.p: Hong Kong's Office of the Telecommunications Authority (OFTA) said on Tuesday it would defer the licensing of cordless access services (CAS) and review the decision in about a year's time.
"The Telecommunications Authority (TA) has decided to defer the licensing of CAS as public telecommunication services," the office said in a statement.
TA invited applications in November 1994 to grant four licences for the provision of CAS in Hong Kong. Six applications were received by the close of the tender on June 30, 1995.
The statement said the deferral should not be seen as a lack of investment interest but rather that prevailing market conditions were not favourable.
Significant reductions in both handset prices and air-time charges of mobile telephones now made CAS less competitive in the mobile phone market, it said.
"The situation would be reviewed in 12 months' time. We shall then decide whether to invite new applications," it said.
